note: Reel 32: Your Body, Right Now (working title). Second-slot pilot, not an episode of the series. The narrator is af_heart, talking to you. In the gaps nobody speaks: the viewer reads a line in their own mother's voice.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: Read this in your mother's voice.
You heard her, didn't you? And I wrote that in English. How many of you heard English?
I've got four of these, and one won't work.
You just checked your back, didn't you?
Now you've embarrassed her in front of guests.
You pay rent, and that still goes straight to your stomach.
Strange, isn't it? Like someone doing an impression of her.
Your brain built that voice out of everything she's ever said to you.
So how many times has she actually said that one?
And how many times has she said this?
Some of you can only hear it this way now.
The rest of you still have the original.
Have you got one recording of her asking?
